name: ESP32-C6

strapping.4: MTMS: SDIO sampling/driving clock-edge strapping together with MTDI/GPIO5 (datasheet v1.5 Table 3-4). Default floating.
strapping.5: MTDI: SDIO sampling/driving clock-edge strapping together with MTMS/GPIO4. Default floating.
strapping.8: Chip boot mode (Joint Download Boot requires GPIO8=1 with GPIO9=0; any value for SPI Boot) and UART0 ROM message printing control with EFUSE_UART_PRINT_CONTROL. Default floating.
strapping.9: Chip boot mode select: 1 = SPI Boot (default, internal weak pull-up), 0 = Joint Download Boot (USB-Serial-JTAG / UART / SDIO download). Holding GPIO9 low at reset enters download mode.
strapping.15: JTAG signal source select, used with EFUSE_DIS_PAD_JTAG / EFUSE_DIS_USB_JTAG / EFUSE_JTAG_SEL_ENABLE (only consulted when JTAG_SEL_ENABLE is burned: 1 = USB Serial/JTAG, 0 = JTAG pins MTDI/MTCK/MTMS/MTDO). Default floating; datasheet: 'This pin does not have any internal pull resistors and the strapping value must be controlled by the external circuit that cannot be in a high impedance state.'

psram.condition: Not applicable: neither the ESP-IDF GPIO summary nor the ESP32-C6 datasheet v1.5 describes a PSRAM interface for this chip.

usb_jtag.note: GPIO12 = USB_D-, GPIO13 = USB_D+. Used by USB-JTAG by default; reconfiguring them as normal GPIOs disables USB-JTAG. If the app reconfigures these pins the device disappears from the host; recover by pulling GPIO9 low and resetting.

notes: flash_spi: ESP-IDF: 'GPIO24 ~ GPIO30 are usually used for SPI flash and not recommended for other uses.' Datasheet: GPIO24/25/26/28/29/30 are the SPI0/1 flash interface; GPIO27 is the VDD_SPI pin ('can only be reconfigured as a GPIO pin if the flash is powered by an external power supply').

Package variants (ESP-IDF): chips with SiP flash built in dedicate GPIO24-GPIO30 to the SiP flash and do not lead out GPIO10-GPIO11 (22 usable GPIOs). Chips without in-package flash do not lead out GPIO14. An auditor should know the exact part number to flag GPIO10/11/14.

input_only / no_internal_pull are empty: ESP-IDF GPIO summary lists none for this chip (the 'input-only GPIOs 34-39' remarks on the page are for the original ESP32); datasheet IO MUX types are I/O/T; TRM v1.2 Register 7.20 IO_MUX_GPIOn_REG (n: 0-30) provides FUN_WPU/FUN_WPD for every GPIO. The datasheet sentence that GPIO15 'does not have any internal pull resistors' describes its reset/strapping state, not a lack of firmware-controllable pulls.
jtag order is [MTMS, MTDI, MTCK, MTDO] = [GPIO4, GPIO5, GPIO6, GPIO7]. JTAG defaults to USB_SERIAL_JTAG; burning DIS_USB_JTAG moves it to GPIO4-GPIO7. GPIO4/GPIO5 are also strapping pins.

No ADC2: datasheet '12-bit SAR ADC, up to 7 channels'; ADC1 CH0-CH6 on GPIO0-GPIO6. ESP-IDF stable ADC oneshot hardware limitations for C6 contain only the RNG and oneshot/continuous exclusivity notes; no Wi-Fi restriction.
LP GPIOs: GPIO0-GPIO7 (LP_GPIO0-7), usable in deep sleep / by LP core. GPIO0/GPIO1 are also XTAL_32K_P/N.
Strapping timing: hold time tH min 3 ms after CHIP_PU high.
Radio: datasheet '2.4 GHz Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax), Bluetooth 5 (LE), Zigbee and Thread (802.15.4)' - no Bluetooth Classic.
Data sourced from ESP-IDF stable = v6.1 docs, ESP32-C6 datasheet v1.5, ESP32-C6 TRM v1.2, retrieved 2026-10-28.
